source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) — IRPS izvensodno reševanje potrošniških sporov, objavljena mnenja
why_relevant: ZBS is the designated ADR body for banking disputes and publishes anonymised opinions plus annual caseload statistics (e.g. ~119 new requests, 133 of 148 open cases resolved in a recent year). Case narratives expose disputed fee, card-fraud and account-access practices bank by category.

source_name: Informacijski pooblaščenec RS (IP) — mnenja ZVOP-2/GDPR database
why_relevant: The DPA's published opinions on bank data processing (ID copies, transaction history access, card data, staff access to accounts) reveal operational practices of Slovenian banks and payment providers that are otherwise undocumented, and flag compliance constraints on data-driven payment products.

source_name: Informacijski pooblaščenec RS — inšpekcijski nadzor / prijava kršitev (enforcement channel)
why_relevant: Pointer to IP's inspection and sanction stream and to its annual report, which aggregates inspection counts by sector including finance/banking — a weak-signal indicator of systemic data practices in payments.

source_name: Sodna praksa RS — iskalnik sodne prakse (case-law search, VS/VSL/VSM/UPRS)
why_relevant: Free national case-law database. Judgments on payment services (ZPlaSSIED), unfair contract terms (ZVPot, OZ), disputed fees and card-fraud liability document how fee and access practices are adjudicated, with facts about specific banks' terms.

source_name: Varuh človekovih pravic RS (Ombudsman) — letna poročila
why_relevant: Ombudsman annual reports carry case narratives on access to banking (basic payment accounts, branch and ATM closures, digital exclusion of elderly/rural users) and have historically flagged unconstitutional banking-law provisions. Weak-signal evidence on cash and branch/ATM access.

source_name: Tržni inšpektorat RS (TIRS) — inspection reports and consumer-protection enforcement
why_relevant: TIRS supervises consumer protection, unfair commercial practices, unfair contract terms and consumer credit (ZPotK). Its annual business reports give inspection and sanction counts by area (13,324 inspections / 6,587 measures reported for 2023), including consumer-credit intermediation adjacent to payments.

source_name: Agencija za trg vrednostnih papirjev (ATVP) — letna poročila and odločitve
source_subtype: financial regulator annual report + decision register
why_relevant: Securities-market regulator supervising banks performing investment services, brokerages and fund managers. Annual reports to Parliament and published decisions (odločitve) reveal sanctions and market-conduct findings against banks; its 'Podatkovno ogledalo' publishes market data.

source_name: PIS — Pravno-informacijski sistem RS (pisrs.si) consolidated legislation register
why_relevant: Authoritative consolidated texts of ZPlaSSIED, ZVPot-1, ZPotK-2, ZPOmK-2 and the emerging cash-access law. Needed to interpret which fee, ATM-coverage and complaint disclosures are legally mandated — i.e. which datasets must exist and be published.

source_name: Uradni list RS — official gazette (incl. commentary on ZDUPS cash/e-payment rules)
why_relevant: Publishes all adopted acts and secondary regulation, including the constitutional amendment on the right to use cash and the payment-means accessibility act; also carries explanatory commentary. Primary record for regulatory shocks to cash/card acceptance and ATM obligations.

source_name: e-Uprava / gov.si — javne obravnave predlogov zakonov (public consultation on ZDUPS cash & basic-account law)
why_relevant: The e-demokracija consultation portal carries draft acts plus stakeholder comments. The ZDUPS draft (ATM within 5 km for settlements >1,000 inhabitants, branch obligation >3,000, free basic package incl. 5 free other-bank ATM withdrawals) is a direct, quantified regulatory constraint on ATM/POS economics; bank and chamber submissions reveal cost data.

source_name: Obrtno-podjetniška zbornica Slovenije (OZS) — merchant-side commentary on payment regulation
why_relevant: Crafts and small-business chamber comments on cash-acceptance and card-acceptance obligations from the merchant/acceptor side, often citing merchant service charges and terminal costs — pricing evidence acquirers do not publish.

source_name: Državni zbor RS — legislative record incl. constitutional article 74.a on the right to use cash
why_relevant: Parliamentary record for the constitutional amendment guaranteeing the right to use cash (new art. 74.a, adopted 67-1) and for the citizens' initiative behind it (56,267 signatures, 'Povezani smo'). Establishes the legal driver for cash-access obligations shaping ATM/branch networks.

source_name: Bank general terms & conditions archives as evidence exhibits (e.g. Intesa Sanpaolo Bank SI, SKB, Gorenjska banka)
why_relevant: Splošni pogoji documents are the artefacts that consumer bodies, inspectors and courts adjudicate; they state ADR routes, fee-change mechanics and card liability rules. Useful as the raw comparison base against ZPS/BS fee comparisons and ADR opinions.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – Zaposlitev (careers / job ads)
why_relevant: Bankart is the national card/ATM/POS/SEPA processor for Slovenia and much of the region. Its job ads name concrete systems, payment instruments and projects (e.g. 'poslovni analitik za razvoj IT storitev na podrocju procesiranja sodobnih placilnih instrumentov', Linux system engineer, development engineer analyst) and therefore reveal technology stack and roadmap direction before any formal announcement. Careers pages also carry self-reported volume claims (cards, monthly SEPA and card transactions, ATM/POS estate) usable as corroborating datapoints for card/ATM/POS statistics.

source_name: Bankart d.o.o. – LinkedIn company page
why_relevant: Company posts announce Flik instant-payment milestones, POS/ATM programme news, partnerships and hiring pushes earlier and more informally than press releases; headcount trend and job-function mix on the page are a proxy for where investment is going.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Zaposlitev / Kariera (central bank job ads)
why_relevant: Central-bank vacancy texts reveal which statistical, oversight and payment-infrastructure workstreams are being staffed up (payment statistics reporting, TARGET/instant payments, digital euro, fintech hub), an early indicator of new reporting obligations and forthcoming statistical products.

source_name: Zavod RS za zaposlovanje (ESS) – national public job vacancy register
why_relevant: Statutory national vacancy register: banks, processors and payment institutions publish here even when they do not advertise commercially. Filtering by NACE banking/finance plus payment keywords gives a systematic, low-bias hiring-signal feed and surfaces smaller actors (payment institutions, e-money issuers) missing from a curated actor map.

source_name: Optius.com – Bancnistvo / Finance job category
why_relevant: Commercial aggregator with a dedicated banking/finance category; useful as a cross-check against ESS and as an actor-discovery channel (vendors, integrators and outsourcers hiring for Slovenian bank projects).

source_name: Zaposlitev.net – Slovenian job portal
why_relevant: Second major commercial aggregator; different employer mix than Optius, so combining the two reduces the chance of missing a bank/processor hiring wave.

source_name: BorzaDela.si – vacancy search (employer-name query)
why_relevant: Small aggregator that indexes by employer name, convenient for monitoring named actors (Banka Slovenije, NLB, Bankart, Halcom) with a single URL pattern per employer.

source_name: Deželna banka Slovenije – Zaposlitve
why_relevant: Smaller domestic bank; its vacancies indicate whether second-tier banks are insourcing or outsourcing card/payment operations, a useful contrast signal to NLB/Bankart activity.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – Napovednik dogodkov (central bank events calendar)
why_relevant: Forward calendar of central-bank conferences, National Payments Council sessions and publication events. Agenda titles disclose upcoming statistical releases and policy themes weeks ahead; pairs with the publication-date calendar for release timing.

source_name: Delo DPC konference – 'Mobilne tehnologije' conference (mobile payments / digital money)
why_relevant: The single most payments-specific recurring Slovenian conference agenda found: the 2026 edition (10 June 2026, Grand Plaza Ljubljana) lists speakers from Banka Slovenije (dr. Marko Pahor), NLB (Sandra Milankovic, director of payment and card services) and Bankart (Samo Kumar) on digital money, neobanks and regulation. Session titles and speaker job titles are a direct read on which institution owns which payments programme, ahead of formal announcements.

source_name: Združenje bank Slovenije (ZBS) – Vsa izobraževanja / strokovna izobraževanja
why_relevant: The banking association's training catalogue and professional meetings (notably the recurring 'posvet o placilnih storitvah' for payment-operations staff) reveal which regulatory and operational changes banks are preparing for — instant payments, PSD2/PSD3, fraud rules — typically before implementation. Course descriptions name the standards and deadlines involved.

source_name: ZBS Bančna konferenca – recorded sessions on YouTube
why_relevant: Full recordings of the annual ZBS banking conference (2023, 2024 editions found). Spoken remarks and presentation slides frequently contain volume figures, cash-usage commentary and project timelines that never appear in written form — a classic weak-signal and last-resort recovery channel.

source_name: Bančni vestnik – e-arhiv (banking journal archive)
why_relevant: The Slovenian banking journal's electronic archive preserves practitioner articles (and English special issues) that often carry payment-system statistics and market descriptions later removed from institutional websites. Acts as the recovery layer for superseded figures.

source_name: Banka Slovenije – 'Arhiv' pages and archived e-newsletters of the National Payments Council
why_relevant: Superseded/archived central-bank content: the National Payments Council e-newsletter archive (e.g. the November 2019 issue on PIS/AIS services) and generic 'Arhiv' sections retain payment-market descriptions and figures dropped from current pages. This is the on-site equivalent of a web archive and is the highest-value recovery target in this cell.
